title: Cooperative puck course
summary: A low-friction puck is already sliding across the table toward the left arm when the episode starts. The two Pandas each hold a paddle and must hit the same puck in turn: left, right, left, right. After each of the first three hits the puck must pass through a different gap in a row of posts standing across the table between the arms. First it goes toward the right arm through the gap at the -y end. Then it goes back toward the left arm through the gap at the +y end, next to a side rail. Then it goes toward the right arm again through the middle gap. The right arm's final hit must send the puck across a goal line in front of a backstop wall on the right arm's side.
robot_setup: panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). Each carries a flat rigid paddle, 0.10 m long (2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.05 m), 0.05 m tall and 12 mm thick, on a rigid adapter on its back (tool -x) side. The tool frame is the paddle centre, with x normal to its faces, y along its length and z up. The TCP sits 0.12 m behind the paddle centre (tool -x) and 0.04 m above it. Left paddle start: centre (-0.05, -0.18, 0.048), orientation identity (faces normal to world x, length along world y). Right paddle start: centre (0.28, 0.12, 0.048), quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) (yawed 180 deg). At the start height each paddle's lower edge is 0.023 m above the table. In this task the servo damping on joints 5-7 is raised to (24, 20, 14) from the default (12, 10, 7). Role labels (panda-0 / panda-1) by phase: left_first_pass striker / preparing_receiver; right_return_route preparing_receiver / striker; left_diagonal_pass striker / preparing_receiver; right_terminal_shot cleared_partner / goal_striker.
scene: A small orange square puck (44 mm x 44 mm, 24 mm tall) slides on the table with very little friction, so it slows down only slowly. At t = 0 it is already moving toward the left arm. A row of four short orange posts stands across the table between the two arms; each post is 32 mm x 50 mm and 70 mm tall. The posts leave three gaps, and they are very bouncy. A long rail, 70 mm tall and also very bouncy, runs along the +y side of the course. A short backstop wall, 0.13 m wide and 70 mm tall and not bouncy, stands behind the goal line on the right arm's side. All of these are fixed, and only the puck moves by itself. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Puck: box 0.044 x 0.044 x 0.024 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.035 kg, friction 0.015, restitution 0.55. At reset it is placed at (0.23, -0.13 + u, 0.0125), with u drawn uniformly in [-0.014, 0.014] m. Its initial velocity is (-`incoming_speed`, 0, 0) = (-0.35, 0, 0) m/s, heading -x through the gap between posts 0 and 1. Table friction `table_friction` = 0.015. Route posts route_post_0..3 are static (friction 0.3, restitution 0.7). Each is 0.032 (x) x 0.050 (y) x 0.070 m, centred at x = 0.12, z = 0.035 and y = -0.22, -0.045, 0.095, 0.26. The resulting gaps are y in [-0.195, -0.07], [-0.02, 0.07] and [0.12, 0.235]. return_rail (static, restitution 0.7): 0.52 x 0.016 x 0.070 m, centred at (0.14, 0.31, 0.035), running along x from -0.12 to 0.40. goal_backstop (static, restitution 0.05): 0.02 x 0.13 x 0.07 m, centred at (0.53, -0.02, 0.035). Paddles: `tool_half` = 0.05, `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, `tool_friction` = 0.3, restitution 0.05. The table top spans x in [-0.54, 0.70] and y in [-0.48, 0.48]. A puck sliding off it falls below z = -0.2 (generic out_of_bounds). Horizon `horizon` = 25 s. The only random draw is u, made at reset.

phases.name: left_first_pass
phases.text: First, a strike by the left paddle is registered: the first moment in this phase when the puck touches the left paddle while the paddle body moves faster than 0.035 m/s, more than 0.06 s after the previous registered strike. Only that first qualifying contact counts as the strike; later touches are allowed but do not register again. Then, more than 0.035 s after the strike and while the puck is not touching the left paddle, the puck's centre crosses the line x = 0.12 moving in +x, with |y - (-0.13)| < 0.055 m. Moving in +x means x was <= 0.12 on the previous physics step and is > 0.12 now. This line passes through the gap between the first and second posts from the -y side.

phases.name: right_return_route
phases.text: A strike by the right paddle is registered under the same rule: the puck touches the right paddle while that paddle moves faster than 0.035 m/s, more than 0.06 s after the previous registered strike. Then, more than 0.035 s after it and while the puck is not touching the right paddle, the puck's centre crosses x = 0.12 moving in -x, with |y - 0.19| < 0.055 m. This is the gap between the third and fourth posts, next to the side rail.

phases.name: left_diagonal_pass
phases.text: A strike by the left paddle is registered (same rule). Then, more than 0.035 s after it and while the puck is not touching the left paddle, the puck's centre crosses x = 0.12 moving in +x, with |y - 0.025| < 0.055 m. This is the middle gap, between the second and third posts.

phases.name: right_terminal_shot
phases.text: A strike by the right paddle is registered (same rule). Then, more than 0.035 s after it and while the puck is not touching the right paddle, the puck's centre crosses x = 0.46 moving in +x, with |y - (-0.02)| < 0.05 m. This is the goal line in front of the backstop. This completes the task.

contact_rules: Each paddle may touch only the puck. The paddles must not touch the posts, the rail, the backstop, the table or the robot pedestals. No other robot part, the fingers included, may touch anything. The two arms and their paddles must never touch each other, and a paddle must not touch its own arm.
world_goals_fixed: The puck's centre must cross three passage lines, given in flag `passages` (not announced in the observation). P0 = (0.12, -0.13), P1 = (0.12, 0.19) and P2 = (0.12, 0.025); each is a crossing of x = 0.12 with |y - y_P| < 0.055 m. The goal line, announced at reset as `goal_goal` = (0.46, -0.02, 0.012), is a crossing of x = 0.46 in +x with |y + 0.02| < 0.05 m.
difficulty_note: The puck slides almost without friction and rebounds hard from the posts and the rail. Every hit must set both speed and direction to thread one particular gap. The paddles must work within a couple of centimetres of a table they may not touch, and the two arms take turns on a puck that travels between them.
standard_notes: The puck is already sliding toward the left arm at t = 0 and keeps sliding for a long time, so it is moving from the very first frame. A paddle touch counts as a strike only while the paddle itself is moving.
